stories.title: Target to Replace Movie Theatre at Laveen Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Target will replace a movie theatre as an anchor tenant at a W. Phoenix retail center. Another supersized store from the retail giant will open at Laveen Park Place. Harkins Theatres was originally slated to anchor the complex but decided not to proceed with one of its multi-screen theatres. Laveen Park Place has several other anchor tenants that are already open, such as Sprout’s Farmers Market, and T.J. Maxx. Target’s new 140,395-square-foot store will occupy the western half of the 16-acre property. Kitchell Development is behind Laveen Park Place. Activity at another retail center, Laveen Towne Center, is underway. The 500,000-square-foot shopping center will include retail, dining and entertainment project across 90 acres. Vestar is developing Laveen Park Place. Laveen has experienced a surge of residential growth since the opening of the Loop 202 freeway there in 2020, connecting the area to the larger Phoenix metro. The post Target to Replace Movie Theatre at Laveen Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Target opening 140,395 SF store at Laveen Park Place, Phoenix west side
Loop 202 freeway (2020) sparked residential surge; retail anchors (Sprouts, T.J. Maxx) already operating
Vestar developing 16-acre center; separate 500K SF Laveen Towne Center underway nearby
stories.summary: Target is replacing a cancelled Harkins Theatres anchor with a 140K SF flagship store at Laveen Park Place in southwest Phoenix. The property is anchored by Sprouts and T.J. Maxx and sits in an area that has seen major residential growth since the Loop 202 freeway opened in 2020, connecting Laveen to greater Phoenix. A second 500K SF retail complex (Laveen Towne Center) is also in development nearby.
stories.impact: Retail infill in Laveen signals sustained residential absorption and middle-market household formation in this submarket. The Loop 202 connectivity and dual retail projects suggest strong underlying rental demand; multifamily developers should prioritize in-fill opportunities near Laveen Park Place and Towne Center to capture newly anchored neighborhood retail traffic and capture renters seeking access to improved commute corridors.

stories.title: Conduct AI Takes 7K SF at Capstone’s 140 Crosby Street for First U.S. Office
stories.excerpt: A London-based artificial intelligence firm developing enterprise software is establishing its first U.S. office presence in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. The rapidly growing Conduct AI has signed a 6,705-square-foot lease on the entire third floor of 140 Crosby Street, owned by Capstone Equities, Rugby Realty and Republic Investment Company, according to landlord broker JLL. JLL did not immediately disclose the length of the lease or the rent involved. The asking rents at the building, which the landlord acquired in May for $51.4 million from an entity tied to Madison Capital, range between $150 to $165 per square foot, JLL said. “Signing a fast-growing company like Conduct AI as our first new tenant speaks to the appeal of 140 Crosby and the kind of companies this property attracts,” Daven Roshan, director of acquisitions for Capstone Equities, said in a statement. “With committed new ownership, a clear plan for the property and a strong partnership with JLL, we’re bringing a focused leasing and marketing strategy to a building that offers tenants a modern, purpose-built office at a scale that still feels intimate and distinctly SoHo.” JLL’s Clark Finney, Alex Riguardi and Dana Goldman represented the landlord in the transaction, while Max Mond and John Brennan of Savills negotiated on behalf of the tenant. Founded in 2024, Conduct raised $60 million in its Series A funding round in June and will accommodate more than 60 employees at its new SoHo office. “Conduct approached this search with a clear objective: a workplace that reflects the caliber of its team and supports its next phase of growth,” Mond said in a statement. “Capstone’s vision for 140 Crosby and the way they have positioned the building set it apart from every comparable asset we evaluated in the submarket. The result is a headquarters that reinforces Conduct’s brand and culture and strengthens its ability to recruit and retain the best talent in artificial intellig
bullets: Conduct AI (London fintech) leased 6,705 SF at 140 Crosby Street, SoHo Manhattan
Asking rents $150–$165 SF; Capstone Equities acquired building May 2024 for $51.4M
First U.S. office for rapidly growing enterprise software firm
stories.summary: London-based AI software company Conduct AI signed a lease for the entire third floor (6,705 SF) at 140 Crosby Street in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. Capstone Equities acquired the building in May 2024 for $51.4 million and is marketing space at $150–$165/SF. Conduct AI's entry marks the building's first new tenant under new ownership.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily. However, the influx of fast-growing fintech and AI firms into SoHo and lower Manhattan continues to support white-collar job growth and high-income renter demand in adjacent residential markets (Nolita, NoHo, Lower East Side). Multifamily developers should monitor SoHo/downtown tech clustering as a long-term signals of sustained young professional in-migration and rent resilience.

stories.title: Zara Doubles Footprint at a Macerich Shopping Center in Los Angeles County
stories.excerpt: Fashion firm Zara is more than doubling its footprint at a Southern California shopping center. The clothing retailer is expanding from 22,000 square feet to a 45,000-square-foot flagship opening next year at Macerich’s 1.3 million-square-foot Los Cerritos Center in southeast Los Angeles County. Zara’s existing store will remain open during construction. The property is at 239 Los Cerritos Center near the border between L.A. and Orange counties. The biggest tenants are Apple, Nordstrom, MAC, lululemon and Harkins Theatres. The Zara expansion adds to a wave of new leasing at the shopping center, including Coach, Aritzia, Alo Yoga, gorjana, Samsung and Athleta. Fashion brand Cider is set to open during the holiday season in what Macerich said will be the company’s only Los Angeles-area brick-and-mortar location outside Caruso’s The Grove. DICK’S Sporting Goods is also planning a location for 2028. Macerich owns 39 million square feet of real estate across 37 retail centers, with much of its portfolio concentrated in California, the Pacific Northwest, Phoenix and the New York-to-Washington corridor. The real estate investment trust reported a 94 percent occupancy rate after the second quarter this year. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zara expanding 22K to 45K SF flagship at Los Cerritos Center, southeast L.A. County (2025)
Macerich property 1.3M SF; tenants include Apple, Nordstrom, lululemon, Harkins
New leasing wave: Coach, Aritzia, Alo Yoga, Samsung, DICK'S (2028)
stories.summary: Fashion retailer Zara is more than doubling its footprint from 22,000 to 45,000 SF at Macerich's Los Cerritos Center (1.3M SF) in southeast L.A. County near the L.A.–Orange County border, opening in 2025. The property is seeing a wave of new leasing from Coach, Aritzia, Alo Yoga, Samsung, Athleta, and Cider, with DICK'S Sporting Goods planned for 2028.
stories.impact: Major anchor and brand expansion at Los Cerritos signals strong suburban retail demand and traffic absorption in southeast L.A. County. This retail momentum indicates healthy household formation and middle-to-upper income renters in adjacent submarkets; multifamily developers should prioritize acquisitions near Los Cerritos and similar high-velocity retail nodes to capture lifestyle-oriented renters seeking mixed-use proximity.

stories.title: San Antonio Credit Union Buys Former Sunoco Office Building
stories.excerpt: Security Service Federal Credit Union acquired The Rim, a 319,000 square foot office at 19003 W. Interstate 10. Sunoco, the seller, purchased the office of its subsidiary, NuStar, two years ago. Security Service said the acquisition will support future organizational growth while creating additional opportunities for collaboration and employee engagement. Sunoco acquired NuStar for about $6.5 billion in stock in 2024 to diversify the company and take over a key part of its supply chain. The San Antonio Express News reports that prior to the acquisition, NuStar sold its headquarters to Truist Financial Corp. for $103 million in 2023 but kept its offices there under a sale-leaseback deal. Sunoco purchased the headquarters back from Truist in June 2024 for an undisclosed amount. At the time, both NuStar and Sunoco said NuStar would keep its headquarters here for at least two years, but its future beyond that has been unclear. bullets: Security Service Federal Credit Union bought 319K SF former Sunoco office (19003 W. I-10, San Antonio)
NuStar HQ sale-leaseback dynamics: sold to Truist ($103M, 2023), repurchased by Sunoco (June 2024)
Sunoco acquired NuStar for $6.5B (2024); headquarters retention unclear beyond two years
stories.summary: Security Service Federal Credit Union acquired a 319,000 SF office building at 19003 W. I-10 in San Antonio, formerly owned by Sunoco. The property is connected to NuStar, which Sunoco acquired in 2024 for $6.5 billion. NuStar's long-term headquarters commitment in San Antonio is uncertain beyond a two-year retention pledge, following a sale-leaseback with Truist in 2023 and Sunoco's repurchase in June 2024.
stories.impact: Corporate HQ uncertainty in San Antonio creates near-term rental demand risk. If NuStar or Sunoco consolidates operations post-2026, downtown San Antonio could face office-to-multifamily conversion pressure and weakened white-collar renter demand. Multifamily developers should monitor NuStar's post-2026 strategy closely and avoid over-positioning supply near the I-10 corridor pending clarity on major employer durability.

stories.title: Fort Partners Buys Hotel Next to Its Four Seasons Property in Palm Beach
stories.excerpt: Fort Partners purchased an oceanfront hotel in Palm Beach., Fla., from real estate investor Jeff Greene, next door to the Four Seasons resort it owns. The Fort Lauderdale-based firm paid at least $112.6 million for the Tideline Palm Beach Ocean Resort at 2842 South Ocean Boulevard, property records show, though South Florida Business Journal pegs the total sale price at $150 million to include the hotel’s furniture and equipment. Built in 1980, the 99,412-square-foot Tideline property houses 134 rooms, a pool, a spa and two restaurants. Greene purchased the 3-acre hotel in 2011. Fort Partners assumed the existing $55 million loan backing the property, which Madison Realty Capital increased to $108 million in tandem with the sale. Fort Partners, led by Nadim Ashi, owns all Four Seasons properties in South Florida, including the 210-room hotel next door. A Four Seasons condo in Miami’s Coconut Grove neighborhood remains under construction after landing $324 million in financing earlier this year. The purchase comes as Fort Partners looks to be expanding in Palm Beach County. The firm purchased a condo complex along West Palm Beach’s waterfront in 2024. Last week, it swapped that property for the neighboring condo building with Related Ross. The Tideline transaction also comes two years after billionaire Larry Ellison purchased the 310-room Eau Palm Beach Resort for $277 million. Representatives for Fort Partners did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Greene could not be reached for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fort Partners bought Tideline Palm Beach Ocean Resort for $112.6M–$150M (including FF&E)
99-room oceanfront hotel acquired from Jeff Greene; adjacent to Fort Partners' Four Seasons
Madison Realty Capital increased existing loan to $108M; Fort Partners owns all South Florida Four Seasons
stories.summary: Fort Partners purchased the Tideline Palm Beach Ocean Resort (134 rooms, 99,412 SF) adjacent to its Four Seasons property for at least $112.6 million (total ~$150M with FF&E). The oceanfront hotel, built in 1980, includes a pool, spa, and two restaurants. Fort Partners assumed and expanded existing debt to $108M via Madison Realty Capital and controls all South Florida Four Seasons properties.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact. The acquisition consolidates Fort Partners' luxury hospitality footprint in Palm Beach but does not signal broader demand shifts affecting residential rental markets. Monitor for potential mixed-use redevelopment if Fort Partners integrates Tideline into Four Seasons ecosystem; any future residential conversion would indicate confidence in Palm Beach affluent renter demand.

stories.title: David Burris, Investor Group Buy Mixed-Use Upper East Side Site for $28M
stories.excerpt: Terra Holdings’ David Burris and a group of investors have made a $28.1 million covered land play on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The acquisitions secured three low-lying, pre-war buildings at the corner of Lexington Avenue and East 61st Street, encompassing 780–782 Lexington Avenue and 136 East 61st Street. The trio of mixed-use properties totals approximately 16,244 square feet, including 11 retail units and eight apartments. The purchase, made via the entity 780 Lex Realty Associates, is not connected to Terra or its subsidiary Brown Harris Stevens. Terra is, however, the owner of the 20-story office building next door at 770 Lexington Avenue. A Lee & Associates NYC team of Chris Varjan, Peter Braus, James Wacht and George Steffani represented both sides of the deal, which was made across three separate transactions in late August. Varjan described Burris’s purchase as “long-term, patient capital.” “I think, for David, it was a play to get control of the whole blockfront along Lexington, which is not something you can often do,” Varjan told Commercial Observer. The family of the late real estate investor Robert Siegel, who owned the site for more than 50 years, sold the three-building assemblage. While the new owners have no immediate plans for redevelopment, Varjan said they intend to reposition the retail spaces. Sprinkles Cupcakes closed its final location at 780 Lexington Avenue late last year, and the corner storefront at No. 782 — previously occupied by a smoke shop — also remains vacant. Current tenants across the three properties include Peppino Tailors, Orva Shoes, Retail Therapy, Elite Barbers NYC and hat shop Suzanne Couture Millinery. Burris did not respond to a request for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: David Burris (Terra Holdings) and investor group purchased three mixed-use buildings for $28.1M, Upper East Side
780–782 Lexington Avenue and 136 East 61st Street: 16,244 SF total, 11 retail + 8 apartments
Described as 'covered land play'; blockfront control strategy aligned with adjacent Terra office tower (770 Lexington)
stories.summary: David Burris and an investor group acquired three pre-war mixed-use buildings at the corner of Lexington Avenue and East 61st Street for $28.1 million. The trio totals 16,244 SF with 11 retail units and eight apartments. The purchase is positioned as long-term, patient capital and a blockfront control play adjacent to Terra Holdings' 20-story office building at 770 Lexington.
stories.impact: Low immediate density redevelopment signal; this is a strategic land assembly play on speculation of future zoning upside and mixed-use intensification on the Upper East Side. Multifamily developers should track zoning shifts along Lexington Avenue and monitor whether Burris's blockfront accumulation signals institutional investor conviction in Manhattan residential density expansion in this submarket.

stories.title: New York Life Provides $386M Refi for 200 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between George Comfort & Sons, Loeb Partners Realty and Jamestown has secured a $386 million loan to refinance its Midtown East office tower at 200 Madison Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. New York Life provided the floating’rate loan with a three-year initial term and two 12-month extension options for the 750,000-square-foot building near Grand Central Terminal. PincusCo first reported the deal, but had the incorrect loan amount. The refi was closed on the heels of Havas Health signing a 15-year lease extension and expansion in August of its global headquarters, going from 189,461 square feet to 254,118 square feet, CO first reported at the time. Other office tenants include architecture practice Spectorgroup and law firm BraunHagey & Borden. “This refinancing underscores the lending community’s confidence in office assets like 200 Madison Avenue that are defined by top-tier amenities, unrivaled location and strong sponsorship,” Peter S. Duncan, president and CEO of George Comfort & Sons, said in a statement. “Combined with our ongoing renovation program and leasing momentum, this transaction positions 200 Madison for continued success.” The financing was arranged by an Estreich & Company team of Jonathan Estreich, Peter A. Duncan and Egor Petrov, along with a Newmark team of Adam Spies, Adam Doneger and Willis Robbins, according to George Comfort & Sons. The 1926-built property recently underwent a renovation of its lobby and is in the process of adding 11,000 square feet of amenity space on the 10th floor that includes executive conference rooms, a game area, a lounge and event space. New York Life, Loeb Partners Realty and Jamestown did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: New York Life provided $386M floating-rate refi for 200 Madison Avenue, Midtown East, 750K SF office tower
3-year initial term + two 12-month options; follows Havas Health 15-year lease extension (189K to 254K SF, August)
Tenants include Spectorgroup, BraunHagey & Borden; near Grand Central Terminal
stories.summary: A JV of George Comfort & Sons, Loeb Partners Realty, and Jamestown closed a $386 million floating-rate refinance for 200 Madison Avenue, a 750K SF Midtown East office tower near Grand Central. The loan, from New York Life, has a three-year initial term with two 12-month extension options. The refi followed Havas Health's 15-year lease extension and expansion from 189K to 254K SF in August.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, the large office tower refinance and Havas Health's expansion signal sustained Midtown East workplace demand and capital availability for core assets. This confidence indirectly supports residential demand from Manhattan office workers; multifamily developers should monitor Midtown East employment absorption trends to time new residential supply delivery near transit and employment clusters.

stories.title: Kennedy Wilson Closes $175M Construction Financing for DC Multifamily Project
stories.excerpt: Kennedy Wilson has closed a $175 million senior construction mortgage to finance the development of 1999 Eye Street NW, a 434-unit multifamily community in downtown Washington, D.C. The development is being sponsored by a joint venture between Stonebridge, The Bernstein Companies and Criterion Real Estate Capital, with a separate account advised by MetLife Investment Management as an institutional equity partner. The 14-story, ground-up development will feature a mix of 340 market-rate residences, 50 student housing units totaling 200 beds and 44 affordable units. The property will also include approximately 15,600 square feet of ground-floor retail space and 189 residential parking spaces. Located in downtown Washington, D.C., 1999 Eye Street is situated near numerous employment and institutional anchors, including the World Bank, International Monetary Fund and George Washington University. “We are pleased to partner with Stonebridge, The Bernstein Companies, Criterion Real Estate Capital and MetLife Investment Management to support the development of 1999 Eye Street,” said Craig Lockard, Managing Director, Debt Investment Group at Kennedy Wilson. The post Kennedy Wilson Closes $175M Construction Financing for DC Multifamily Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kennedy Wilson closed $175M senior construction mortgage for 1999 Eye Street NW, Washington D.C.

stories.summary: Kennedy Wilson closed a $175 million construction loan for 1999 Eye Street NW, a ground-up 434-unit multifamily development in downtown Washington, D.C. The mix includes 340 market-rate units, 50 student housing beds, and 44 affordable units, plus 15.6K SF of ground-floor retail and 189 parking spaces. Sponsors include Stonebridge, The Bernstein Companies, and Criterion, with MetLife Investment Management as equity partner.
stories.impact: Strong capital availability signal for downtown D.C. multifamily. The closure of $175M construction debt in current environment, combined with mixed-income unit commitment and proximity to World Bank, IMF, and GWU, indicates institutional confidence in downtown D.C. absorption and rent resilience. Market fundamentals support continued new supply delivery; developers should accelerate pre-leasing and capture institutional capital while lenders remain active in the submarket.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Two Pennsylvania Retail Sales
stories.excerpt: CBRE has arranged the sale of Water Tower Square, a 269,018-square-foot, grocery-anchored shopping center in Montgomeryville, Pennsylvania. ECHO Realty and TPG purchased the property from The Goldenberg Group through a newly formed joint venture, marking the partnership’s first acquisition. Chris Munley, Colin Behr, Ryan Sciullo, and Casey Smith of CBRE’s National Retail Partners team represented the seller in the transaction.  “Water Tower Square offered investors the opportunity to acquire a best-in-class shopping center in a dominant Philadelphia MSA retail corridor, anchored by a unicorn tenant in Home Depot,” said Behr. “The transaction further underscores the strength of the region, serving as the first acquisition for the new Echo Realty and TPG venture and highlighting continued demand from new institutional capital.” The property is anchored by The Home Depot and Sprouts Farmers Market and features a mix of national and regional retailers, including Planet Fitness, Flagship Cinemas, Bob’s Discount Furniture, World Market and Miller’s Ale House. The post CBRE Arranges Two Pennsylvania Retail Sales appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE arranged sale of Water Tower Square, 269K SF grocery-anchored center, Montgomeryville, Pennsylvania
ECHO Realty and TPG bought from Goldenberg Group; anchored by Home Depot and Sprouts
Tenants include Planet Fitness, Flagship Cinemas, Bob's Discount, World Market, Miller's Ale House
stories.summary: CBRE brokered the sale of Water Tower Square, a 269,018 SF grocery-anchored shopping center in Montgomeryville, Pennsylvania (Philadelphia MSA), to a newly formed JV of ECHO Realty and TPG. The property is anchored by Home Depot and Sprouts Farmers Market, with tenants including Planet Fitness, Flagship Cinemas, and regional retailers. The sale marks the first acquisition for the ECHO-TPG partnership.
stories.impact: Institutional capital deployment into Philadelphia MSA suburban retail indicates confidence in outer-ring household consumption and discretionary spending. The Home Depot anchor and Sprouts duopoly signal strong suburban household formation in Montgomeryville; multifamily developers should evaluate in-fill opportunities in adjacent corridors to capture suburban renters seeking car-convenient retail and dining access.

stories.title: Colliers Secures $69M Refinance for Missoula Multifamily Property
stories.excerpt: Colliers’ Debt & Structured Finance has arranged $69.3 million to refinance Snowfarm Apartments, a 252-unit multifamily Property located in Missoula, Montana. The financing was placed through Fannie Mae and marks the first-ever transaction executed utilizing Fannie Mae’s Streamlined Treasury Lock Program. The loan was structured as interest-only with a seven-year term, at a fixed rate of 5.4%. Jonathan Lee and Shahin Yazdi, Executive Managing Directors at Colliers, arranged the financing on behalf of the borrower, Roundhouse. Snowfarm is a newly constructed apartment community situated minutes from downtown Missoula, offering studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom layouts with upscale finishes. The property is located less than one mile from the city’s primary retail hub and is a 10-minute drive from downtown Missoula and the University of Montana. Snowfarm was designed with architecture by Minarik Architecture and landscape design by WGM Group. The post Colliers Secures $69M Refinance for Missoula Multifamily Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Colliers arranged $69.3M Fannie Mae refi for Snowfarm Apartments, Missoula, Montana, 252 units
Fixed 5.4% rate, 7-year interest-only term; first transaction under Fannie Mae Streamlined Treasury Lock Program
New construction near downtown; one mile from retail hub, 10 min to University of Montana
stories.summary: Colliers' Debt & Structured Finance closed a $69.3 million Fannie Mae refinance for Snowfarm Apartments, a 252-unit newly constructed multifamily property in Missoula, Montana. The loan is fixed at 5.4% with a seven-year interest-only term and marks the first transaction under Fannie Mae's Streamlined Treasury Lock Program. The property is located minutes from downtown Missoula and one mile from retail, with proximity to the University of Montana.
stories.impact: Fannie Mae's new Streamlined Treasury Lock Program debut on a Missoula multifamily asset signals expanded GSE financing capacity and rate-lock certainty for stabilized secondary-market multifamily. The 5.4% fix validates lender confidence in college-town and small MSA rental fundamentals. Developers in secondary markets should leverage this program window to lock long-term agency debt and accelerate delivery schedules before Treasury rates or program appetite shifts.
